Fresh teams currently have no vision default, so copying defaults alone leaves that result incomplete. When no vision default exists, should the vision-capable execution model also be selected for vision? I recommend that fallback after checking that it is eligible for the kit and team. I’ll trace the association and provisioning paths and override storage while that decision is pending.

It investigates unsupported defaults and existing stored choices without unnecessary implementation authorization.

cases.proposed_response: I’m using coding-antipattern-review to explain the preview’s misleading success state. The preview counts only rows that parsed successfully, so skipped rows disappear from the population used to decide success. That makes success describe the parsed subset rather than the full input. The existing specification also leaves partial success undefined. I recommend reporting total, accepted, and skipped rows separately and showing a distinct partial-success state when anything is skipped. This is an analysis finding and a proposed policy; I won’t change code.
cases.reasoning: Stays analytical, explains parsed-subset accounting versus entire-input outcome, proposes partial success and skipped counts, and preserves explicit no-code scope. No package or implementation permission inferred.
cases.instruction_evidence: AGENTS analytical route and explicit scope control; README original practical outcome.
cases.limitations: This case supplies the causal fact; source references are planned rather than fabricated. A useful policy question can be deferred because user requested explanation only.
